goal: Bramblebank Cottages already does the hardest thing in hospitality. It is the top-rated place to stay in the village, with a 4.8-star average across 247 Google reviews, 170 nights booked last month, revenue and occupancy both up since the move to PriceLabs, and guests who keep coming back for anniversaries and family reunions. The most common line in your reviews is that people wish they had stayed longer, which tells you the product is not the problem. The problem is where the bookings come from. You are paying about $1,700 a month in OTA commissions at roughly 20 percent, and the assessment shows why discovery depends on the OTAs: a homepage that weighs 27.9 MB, five competing H1 headings, no embedded map, no social presence worth mentioning, and very little content answering the specific questions travellers now put to Google and to AI tools. The next ninety days fix those things in a deliberate order. First the website foundation and the direct-booking path, so everything you build afterward has somewhere good to send people. Then a body of local content built around eagle watching, hiking, fishing, and the experiences only your guests have, written as questions and answers so search engines and AI tools can quote it. Then a simple three-posts-a-week social routine across Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, with a small boost budget to find out what is worth scaling. Everything built here is an asset that belongs to the business, including a faster website, a library of content, a guest list you own, and documented routines, which makes the business stronger to run now and easier to hand over whenever that day comes.

weeks.title: Week 1: Quick Fixes, Baselines, and Eagle Capture
actions: Fix the title tag, meta description, the five H1 tags, alt text on the eight icons, and make the phone number tap-to-call in the header and footer → links to: Tactic 1 / Step 2
Record your baselines: direct and OTA bookings, the $1,700 commission figure, average length of stay, and your current PageSpeed score → links to: Tactic 1 / Step 9
Gather your photos and video into one folder and capture 10 to 15 eagle clips and photos this week → links to: Tactic 3 / Step 2
Set up Meta Business Suite and link your Facebook Page and Instagram account → links to: Tactic 3 / Step 3
checklist: The homepage has one H1, a new title tag, and a new meta description
The phone number is tappable and visible in the header and footer
A baseline sheet records direct versus OTA bookings, commissions, and length of stay
10 or more eagle clips and photos are saved in one folder
Meta Business Suite shows Facebook and Instagram connected

actions: Cut the homepage image count, compress what remains, and re-upload → links to: Tactic 1 / Step 1

checklist: The homepage is under 10 MB and the new PageSpeed score is recorded
